title: Checkerboards in any proportion
summary: Start with a standard board, then set the rows, columns, colors and box shape, such as 3:1 or 2:3.

body.text: The new [checkerboard maker](/checkerboards/) opens on a standard 8 by 8 board. From there, you can stretch the boxes and shift the rows.

items.caption: Boxes three times as wide as tall
A 2:3 brick pattern in three colors

Two to four colors, with every palette on the site

title: Crochet colorwork squares, written out in full
summary: Tapestry crochet charts, corner-to-corner graphs and granny squares in your colors, with every row, diagonal and round written out in US terms.

body.text: [Crochet colorwork](/crochet/colorwork/) is a new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/), with nine original designs across three techniques. Pick one, set your colors, and get a complete square from the starting chain to blocking.

items.caption: A stepped cross in tapestry crochet
The chart for a corner-to-corner heart
A granny square in six rounds
A four-color granny square in DK yarn

items: Tapestry crochet: a chart with row numbers and a color key, which way each row reads, how to carry the unused yarn, and color changes on the last yarn-over
Corner-to-corner: increasing then decreasing diagonals, the block count and block colors for each diagonal, and how many yarn bobbins to wind
Granny squares: stitch counts for every round, corners, and joining a new color
Every square: an edging, fastening off, weaving in, blocking, gauge notes, yarn per color that adds up to the total, and a printable PDF

body.text: Color A is the main color and the edging, and the others are contrasts. Use any palette, and a share link keeps your colors, yarn weight and size. Yardage is a rough estimate, so check it against your own swatch.

title: Charted knit colorwork, written out as complete squares
summary: Thirteen original stranded, mosaic and intarsia charts, fitted to your gauge, with every row written color by color.

body.text: [Knit colorwork](/knitting/colorwork/) is a new tool in the [pattern library](/patterns/). Each chart was drawn for this site and is written out as a complete square, from cast on to blocking, at your size and gauge.

items.caption: Little Pines, stranded in two yarns
Ribbon Chevron, a stranded chart in three yarns
Mosaic Diamonds, with one yarn in each row

items: A chart with a color key and row numbers on the side each row starts from
Written rows, color by color, in working order
Repeats fitted to your stitch count, with matching edges and a garter border
A float check that flags any row carrying a yarn more than about an inch at your gauge
Yarn estimated per color, adding up to the total
A printable PDF, plus SVG and PNG of the square and chart

body.text: Colorwork rarely matches the gauge of plain knitting, so each pattern asks for a swatch of its own chart. Enter what you measure, and the square, rows, floats and yarn all change to match. If you want one color instead, the [knitting stitches](/knitting/) are still there.

title: Draw fractals from one simple rule
summary: Nine classic fractals at the depth you choose, in your colors or as black lines, with SVG, PNG and PDF downloads.

body.text: The new [fractal maker](/fractals/) repeats a simple rule as many times as you ask, and each kind of fractal has [its own page](/fractals/hilbert-curve/).

items.caption: A Pythagoras tree leaning at 40 degrees
A Koch snowflake in black lines

SVG and PNG downloads, and a printable PDF with a black-line page

title: Mazes as big as your wall
summary: Choose exact columns and rows, up to 400 by 400, then download a poster PDF up to 4A0 or a PNG up to 16384 pixels.

body.text: The [maze generator](/mazes/) now takes the columns and rows you choose, and it prints as large as your printer can go.

title: Generate a printable maze with one true path
summary: Pick a shape, an algorithm and a difficulty, then print the maze with its solution on a separate page.

body.text: The [maze generator](/mazes/) is a new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Every maze it draws has exactly one route between any two cells, with no loops and no walled-off areas.

items.caption: A circular maze from Wilson's algorithm
An easy hexagonal maze from Prim's algorithm
A square maze from Kruskal's algorithm, with its solution
A rectangular binary tree maze, with its diagonal lean

items: Four shapes: square, rectangle, circle and hexagon
Five algorithms with different textures: recursive backtracker, Prim, Kruskal, Wilson and binary tree
Six difficulties, from easy to extreme, which set how many cells the maze has
A printable PDF with the solution on its own page
SVG and PNG of the maze and of its solution, with your wall weight and colors

body.text: A seed picks the maze: the same seed and settings always draw the same one. Your browser remembers your seed and the PDF prints it. Share links keep your settings but not the seed, so to draw the same maze elsewhere, type the seed in.

title: Plan a tie-dye before you pick up the dye
summary: Preview a spiral, bullseye or accordion fold in your colors, then get the folds, a dye map, mixing amounts and printable steps.

body.text: The new [tie-dye planner](/tie-dye/) previews a design in your colors, and tells you how to fold it and how much dye to mix.

items.caption: An eight-ring bullseye in two dyes
The folds and dye map for an accordion

items: Spiral, bullseye and accordion folds with up to four dyes
A preview as SVG or PNG, and a fold diagram with a map of where each dye goes
Water, powder and urea amounts for up to 12 adult T-shirts
A printable PDF with the safety notes and every step from soak to wash

body.text: Real dye spreads differently every time, so treat the picture as a guide. The amounts are estimates scaled from [Dharma Trading's published instructions](https://www.dharmatrading.com/blogs/t/tie-dye-instructions), and your dye's label comes first.

title: Cross stitch and needlepoint, now complete projects
summary: Needlepoint has its own maker, and both tools now give everything for a finished square piece: exact cut, stitching order, thread per color, finishing, and charts split over sheets.

body.text: Needlepoint now has [its own maker](/needlepoint/), apart from the [cross-stitch maker](/cross-stitch/). Both give full instructions for a finished square piece, not just a chart, and both have six new complete designs with borders, drawn for this site.

items.caption: Tree of life on 18-count fabric, as a pillow
Seaside sun on canvas, in continental stitch
Flame square in Persian yarn on 18-mesh canvas

items: The exact size of fabric or canvas to cut, and how to find and mark the center
A stitching order by color, with the square to start each color on
Strands, yards and a skein estimate per color
Framing or pillow steps, with every size worked out
PDF charts split over sheets when they're large, with overlapping rows and center arrows

body.text: Choose canvas mesh from 10 to 18, then basketweave, continental or half-cross tent stitch, and tapestry wool or Persian yarn. Yarn estimates follow the stitch and the yarn. The canvas gets a margin for blocking and finishing, the work order leaves the background until last, and blocking comes before making up. Old needlepoint links from the cross-stitch page open on the new page.

title: Every crochet stitch now writes a complete square
summary: Pick a crochet stitch and a square size to get the whole pattern: materials, foundation chain, every row, an edging, and finishing.

body.text: The [crochet stitch pages](/crochet/) used to give you a few rows to repeat. Each one now writes a whole square, such as a washcloth or an afghan square, in US terms, on the page and in the PDF.

items.caption: A 12" square in back loop rib

items: Materials: yarn weight, hook size, estimated yardage, notions, gauge, finished size, and an abbreviations key
An exact foundation chain, with how each stitch's turning chain counts
Row 1 and Row 2 written out with their stitch counts, then an exact number of repeats that ends on a wrong-side row
One round of single crochet edging, with 3 stitches in each corner and a count for every side
How to fasten off, weave in the ends, and block

body.text: Choose a 6, 8, 10 or 12 inch square, or set your own width and length. The edging counts toward the finished size, and the row count is worked out from your gauge so the piece comes out square. As always, swatch first: these numbers are only right at your gauge.

title: Knit a complete square in any stitch
summary: Every knitting stitch page now writes out a whole square at your gauge: materials, cast on, border, every row, bind off and blocking.

body.text: Each stitch in the [knitting library](/knitting/) now gives you a complete pattern for a square, such as a dishcloth or an afghan square, instead of only the rows that repeat. Pick 6, 8, 10 or 12 inches, enter your gauge, and the pattern is written for those numbers.

items.caption: A 12 inch square in seed stitch
A 6 inch square in stockinette, kept flat by its border

items: Yarn weight, needle size, estimated yardage, notions and abbreviations
Gauge and finished size, with a cast-on count that fits the stitch's repeat
A garter stitch border on all four sides, to stop curling
Numbered rows, an exact repeat count that ends on a wrong-side row, and stitch count checks along the way
Binding off, weaving in the ends and blocking
All of it in the printable PDF, and in the share link

body.text: The written rows come from the same chart as the stitch's preview. Our tests follow each pattern row by row at many sizes and gauges, counting every stitch and checking that the finished piece is within one repeat of square. Your own swatch still decides the real size, so measure it first.

body.text: The [mandala maker](/mandalas/) now builds a design ring by ring, the [palette page](/palettes/) groups colors by theme and harmony, and the [pattern library](/patterns/) shows several patterns of every type.

items.caption: Six rings chosen by hand, in 16-fold symmetry
A seeded coloring page using four of the new motifs

Drag rings to reorder them and drag motifs onto rings, with buttons that do the same from the keyboard or a touch screen

body.text: Switching language now changes one secondary color instead of the whole look. The site's main colors and each design's primary colors stay the same.

title: Make seamless patterns from one turning tile
summary: Pick a tile, a grid and a layout, then download a seamless SVG or PNG repeat or a printable PDF.

body.text: The [Truchet tile maker](/truchet/) is a new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/). It fills a grid with one simple tile, turned a different way from place to place, and the turns make the pattern.

items: Four tiles: quarter arcs, straight chamfers, diagonal lines and diagonal triangles
Random, mirrored, checkerboard, stripe and diagonal wave layouts
A seamless repeat, as SVG or PNG
A printable PDF with one repeat at true size and a full sheet of repeats

body.text: Random layouts come from a seed, so the same seed always gives the same pattern. Your browser remembers your last seed, but links don't carry it.

title: Draw true girih and geometric star patterns
summary: Build a repeating patch from the five girih tiles, or a star pattern on regular polygons, then download a seamless repeat, a stencil, a wall panel and a printable PDF.

body.text: The [geometric stars and girih maker](/girih/) comes from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Its 10-fold option uses the five girih tiles: decagon, pentagon, bowtie, rhombus and elongated hexagon. Every edge is the same length, and lines cross each edge's midpoint at 72 and 108 degrees.

items: A seamless repeat, as SVG or PNG
A wall panel of repeats inside a plain border
A stencil whose bands hold the sheet in one piece, with holes for lining it up
A printable PDF with the panel, one repeat, the stencil and notes

body.text: Only the 10-fold option is called girih. The 4, 6, 8 and 12-fold options are geometric star patterns on regular polygons. An 8, 10 or 12-fold star can't give a whole repeating pattern that symmetry, so the tool lists the star's rotation and the pattern's separately. The girih patch came from a computer search and isn't copied from any building.

title: Generate geometric radial designs and coloring pages
summary: Choose a symmetry, rings, motifs and colors to generate an original radial design, then download it in color or as a coloring page.

body.text: The [mandala maker](/mandalas/) generates geometric radial designs from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Pick 6 to 24 folds of symmetry, 2 to 8 rings, and the motifs each ring may use: petals, arcs, dots, scallops, diamonds or triangles.

items: A colored design, as SVG or PNG
A black-on-white coloring page, as SVG or PNG
A printable PDF with the colored design and the coloring page
A share link that reopens the same design

body.text: The same seed and settings always give the same design. These are generated shapes: they don't copy a traditional design, and they carry no intended meaning.

title: Design a stained glass panel and print its cutting templates
summary: Choose a design, size, came and colors, then print numbered true-size templates with the came allowance already applied.

body.text: The [stained glass pattern maker](/stained-glass/) is a new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Choose one of four original designs, set the panel size and your came, and pick four glass colors.

items.caption: The numbered key for a border and center

items: A PDF with a numbered key and true-size templates, with the came allowance applied and a 1 inch check square on every template sheet
Pieces too big for a page tiled over taped sheets, and listed as such
A rough glass estimate for each color, including a stated 30% waste allowance
A panel preview as SVG or PNG

body.text: Strict about what can be cut

A score only runs straight from edge to edge, so every piece has straight sides and no inside corners. No corner is under 30 degrees, cut glass is at least 3/4" wide, and long pieces are split. If a design breaks a rule at your size, the tool lowers the detail and tells you. These limits are cautious guidance, not a guarantee, and the estimates are rough, so verify with your came and your supplier.

title: Make a Celtic knot for a laser, a stencil or a coloring page
summary: Build an interlaced knot on a grid, add breaks, and download a cut file, a tattoo stencil, a coloring page, a PNG or a printable PDF.

body.text: The [Celtic knot maker](/celtic-knots/) is a new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Pick a grid size and a break pattern, and it traces the strands into closed loops that go over and under in turn.

items.caption: A frame with interlace off, as a coloring page

items: SVG cut files of closed, filled shapes for a laser or Cricut
A tattoo stencil of ribbon edges, with gaps at each under-crossing
A coloring page with black outlines on white
PNG images and a printable PDF

body.text: Random patterns come from a seed, so the same seed always gives the same knot. Your browser remembers your last seed, but links don't carry it. Mirrored, rotated and fixed patterns are symmetric. You can give each strand its own color, and the page tells you how many strands your design has.

title: Print a true-size sashiko stitch guide
summary: Choose a geometric motif, a grid size and a panel size, then print a true-size guide with gaps laid out at the crossings.

body.text: The [sashiko stitch guide maker](/sashiko/) draws geometric motifs as dashed stitch lines, ready to print and transfer to your cloth. Choose asanoha, seigaiha, shippo, kikko, kagome or a simple grid, then set the grid size, stitch length, panel size and colors.

items: A true-size PDF, tiled across letter sheets when the panel is larger than one, with a 1 inch check square on each sheet
Stitches centered on each line, so gaps fall at the crossings and stitches don't cross there
An SVG and PNG of the panel in your cloth and thread colors
A rough stitch count and thread estimate

body.text: Sashiko is a Japanese stitching tradition with its own teachers and many ways of working. This tool only draws line guides, and it makes no claims about where a motif comes from. The stitch length and gap are a starting point, so adjust them to your thread, cloth and hand.

title: Make a tessellation in any of the 17 wallpaper groups
summary: Choose a motif, a wallpaper group and your colors, then download a seamless repeat, a tile layout and a printable PDF.

body.text: The [tessellation maker](/tessellations/) is a new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Pick a motif, choose one of the 17 wallpaper groups, and set three colors.

items: A seamless repeat, as SVG or PNG
A tile layout, as SVG or PNG, that marks each repeat and one tile
A printable PDF with the layout, the group's symmetry and one repeat

body.text: The five hexagonal groups have no square repeat. Their smallest upright rectangle is about 1.73 times as tall as it is wide, so that's the shape of the file you download. Tests check each group's rotations, mirrors and glides, and that every repeat meets itself at its edges.

title: Make a printable cross-stitch or needlepoint chart
summary: Choose or draw a motif, set your fabric count and colors, and get a symbol chart, stitch counts, a rough thread estimate and the finished size.

body.text: The [cross-stitch and needlepoint maker](/cross-stitch/) is new in the [pattern library](/patterns/). Start from a motif or draw your own on the grid, then choose your colors and fabric count.

items: A printable PDF chart, with a symbol for each color and a heavy line every 10 stitches
A color list with the stitch count for each color
A rough thread estimate for each color
The finished size at your fabric count, and how much fabric to cut

body.text: Colors are plain colors you choose, not matched to any thread brand, so pick the closest thread you have. The motifs were drawn for this site.

title: Design a plaid and get a weaving guide
summary: Set your thread colors and counts to make a balanced plaid, then download a seamless swatch and a printable weaving guide.

body.text: The [tartan and plaid maker](/tartans/) is the first new tool from the [pattern library](/patterns/). Choose thread colors and counts, mirror them if you like, and see the cloth woven in 2/2 twill.

items: A seamless repeat, as SVG or PNG
The thread order to wind and weave
Warp ends and weft picks for your cloth size
A rough yarn estimate for each color, and a printable PDF guide

body.text: The presets are invented for this site. Some tartans are restricted or belong to a family or organization, so named historic tartans will be added only with documented sources.

title: Endless Patterns now speaks five languages
summary: The site is now in English, Spanish, French, German and Brazilian Portuguese, with colors that shift a little for each.

body.text: Every page, cutting list, row instruction and PDF is now available in [Español](/es/), [Français](/fr/), [Deutsch](/de/) and [Português](/pt/). Use the language links at the top of any page to switch.
Each language gets a subtle shift in the site's colors and default palette, loosely inspired by a flag commonly associated with it. Each sample below opens in that language.

These translations are a first draft and haven't been reviewed by crafters yet. Block and stitch names stay in English, measurements stay in inches and yards, and needle and hook sizes use US numbering. Crochet uses local abbreviations, with the US term in parentheses.

title: A blog and changelog for what's new
summary: New features now get a post with samples you can open and change, and every update goes in the changelog.

body.text: Endless Patterns now has this blog and a [changelog](/changelog/). The changelog is the short list of what changed and when. Blog posts are for bigger additions, with examples you can try.
Samples you can open and change
Each sample in a post is a link into the matching tool, with the same settings already filled in. Open one, then change the size, colors or gauge to make it your own.
